question: Which of the following statements is correct about the concept of 'molecules of compounds'?

options.text: A molecule of a compound is formed by the separation of atoms of the same element.
A molecule of a compound is formed by the combination of atoms of different elements.
A molecule of a compound is formed by the combination of atoms of the same element.
A molecule of a compound is formed by the separation of atoms of different elements.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A molecule of a compound is formed by the combination of atoms of different elements.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **A molecule of a compound** is formed by the **chemical combination of atoms of different elements**. These atoms join in fixed proportions to form a compound. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• A molecule of a compound is **not formed by the separation of atoms**, whether they are of the same or different elements. This concept contradicts the definition of a compound. *Hence, statements mentioning separation are incorrect.*
 
• Atoms of the **same element form molecules of elements**, not compounds. For example, O₂ and H₂ are molecules of elements, not compounds. *Hence, the option "combination of atoms of the same element" is incorrect.*
 
• Compounds have **distinct chemical properties** that are different from the properties of the individual elements that constitute them. This is due to the chemical bonding between different types of atoms.
